name: Shaul
title: Israel's First King
summary: Shaul (Saul) was the first king of united Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel after the people demanded a monarch. He began as a humble and promising leader, but his disobedience to God led to him losing the kingdom to David. His reign was marked by military victories, but also by jealousy, instability, and ultimately a tragic death on Mount Gilboa.

keyEvents.title: Saul Anointed as King
keyEvents.description: The prophet Samuel anointed Saul in secret to become Israel's first king by God's command, after the people demanded a king like other nations.

keyEvents.title: Saul Chosen Publicly by Lot
keyEvents.description: At a public gathering in Mizpah, Saul was chosen as king by lot, and the people shouted: "Long live the king!"

keyEvents.title: Victory over the Ammonites
keyEvents.description: Saul gathered Israel's army and defeated the Ammonites at Jabesh Gilead, which strengthened his position as king.

keyEvents.title: Saul Offers Sacrifice Illegally at Gilgal
keyEvents.description: Saul did not wait for Samuel and offered a burnt offering himself before the battle against the Philistines. Samuel declared that Saul's kingdom would not endure because of his disobedience.

keyEvents.title: Saul Spares King Agag
keyEvents.description: After defeating the Amalekites, Saul spared King Agag and kept the best of the livestock, contrary to God's command. Samuel declared that the Lord had rejected Saul as king.

keyEvents.title: Saul's Death on Mount Gilboa
keyEvents.description: In the decisive battle against the Philistines on Mount Gilboa, Saul's sons fell, and Saul took his own life by throwing himself on his sword to avoid being captured.
